# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-10 (Extended v95)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Spring Year 3 to Summer Year 3, dual settings)**: (1) Paris, le Petit-Picpus convent district—Valjean and Cosette in sanctuary within walled convent garden; (2) English provincial harbor towns and hill farms (Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Staveford, Ravenmere, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Dunby, Dungate, Torton) with multiple inhabitants engaged in seasonal activities. Key historical dates: 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, Valjean's theft and flight; Waterloo/Hougomont); 1817 (young Parisians' excursion; M. Gillenormand began frequenting Madame de T.'s salon twice weekly in Rue Férou); 1818 spring (Montfermeil, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral tenure); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest, trial, Valjean's self-revelation, Fantine's death, Valjean's escape)**; **December 1823 (Montfermeil rescue of Cosette, 1,500-franc payment to Thénardier; December 26 return to Paris)**; 1824 spring onward (decrepit building lodging; winter passed); **Summer Year 2 (achieved sanctuary in convent)**; **Winter Year 2 (Mother Crucifixion died, funeral, vault burial)**; **Spring Year 3 (currently occurring)**; **Summer Year 3 (explicitly noted as "summer of the third year")**.

## Primary Locations

**PARIS - LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; market-gardens, timber-yards, unpaved rut-filled roads. **Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus (convent carriage gate)**: Ajar gate, courtyard, vine-hung walls, tall trees above 18-foot wall. **Convent complex—three buildings**: (1) **Great Convent** (Bernardines-Benedictines nuns; gloomy, heavily shuttered); (2) **Boarding-school** (scholar lodging); (3) **Little Convent** (aged nuns of various orders, destroyed in Revolution). **Interior garden**: Vast oblong with poplar alley, forest trees, gnarled fruit-tree, vegetable beds, melon patch with glass frames, old well, stone benches, grass, green mould. **Parlor (Great Convent)**: Monstrous iron lattice with black shutters (always closed). **Chapel**: Window visible from garden; nuns perform prayer/reparation. **Burial location**: Mother Crucifixion's vault beneath grand altar (concealed, no government suspicion). **Vaugirard cemetery**: Ancient burial ground with special Prefecture Permission for nightfall interments.

**ENGLISH PROVINCIAL SETTINGS**: Multiple named locations with ordinary inhabitants. **Weather/seasonal conditions (Spring to Summer Year 3)**: Roads all ruts and puddles after thaw; frost silvered hedges; bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage; children chased hoops down lanes; bell for vespers rang thinly across roofs; light went early; smoke from chimneys lay flat over fields; wind off water with salt/tar smell; rain threatened morning but held off. **Population movements**: Yera Haskick left Dunstead, settled Kelmere; Rinelle quit Kelford for Torton; Kadrek Brackick followed to Torton; Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged; Luena packed trunk, moved Staveford to Dungate; Rozek Stenenridge followed Luena to Dungate within month; Volan Stenworth mended torn sleeve by window, said little.

**GORBEAU HOVEL (50-52)**: Salpêtrière district, outskirts Paris. Eternally posted "Chambers to let"; presently inhabited by numerous indigent individuals from class separating from lowest petty bourgeoisie down to sewer-men and rag-pickers. **Current tenant—Jondrette family**: Father hired chamber, stated name "Jondrette" upon hiring; entrance resembled "entrance of nothing at all"; instructed portress to respond affirmatively if inquired for Pole, Italian, or Spaniard.

**M. GILLENORMAND'S HOUSEHOLD**: **Rue Boucherat, Rue de Normandie, Rue de Saintonge** (ancient residents remember him); now lives in **Rue Servandoni** (no longer), currently maintains **Rue Férou residence** (neighborhood). Doors absolutely closed during day; never receives anyone except evening; dines at five o'clock; after that door opens. Antiquated elegance philosophy: "Day is vulgar, deserves only closed shutter. Fashionable people only light up minds when zenith lights stars."

## Jean Valjean's Psychological and Spiritual Development

**ESCAPE EXECUTION**: Hid inside coffin before Fauchelevent nailed upper plank; demonstrated gloomy talent—understood contracting to fit diameter; could economize breath for hours without dying; possessed composure and coolness contagious to others.

**CURRENT STATUS (Spring-Summer Year 3)**: Integrated into convent life as assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Works in garden daily; formerly pruner of trees; knows agricultural secrets; budded ungrafted orchard trees producing excellent fruit. Receives daily visits from Cosette (appointed hour); watches her running/playing; distinguishes her laugh.

**SPIRITUAL TRANSFORMATION**: During night meditations rose to listen to grateful song of innocent nuns; blood ran cold—justly chastised raised voices only in blasphemy while he, wretch, had shaken fist at God. Realized: scaling wall made to escape other place of expiation now served entrance to this one. Was this symbol of his destiny? Pride vanished. Scrutinized own heart; felt pettiness; wept many times. All entering life last six months led back towards Bishop's holy injunctions—Cosette through love, convent through humility. Sometimes at eventide knelt in middle of walk skirting chapel, prostrated in prayer. Everything surrounding him—peaceful garden, fragrant flowers, children's joyous cries, grave and simple women, silent cloister—slowly permeated him. Soul became compounded of silence, perfume, simplicity, joy. Reflected: two houses of God received him at critical moments—first when all doors closed (society rejected him); second when society pursued him (galleys yawning). Without first, relapsed into crime; without second, into torment.

## Cosette's Integration and Development

**INITIAL STATE**: Knew nothing; could say nothing. Unhappiness trained her to silence. Suffered much; feared everything, even to speak/breathe. Hardly begun regaining confidence since with Jean Valjean.

**CONVENT INTEGRATION**: Speedily became accustomed; only regretted Catherine but dared not say so. Once told Valjean: "Father, if I had known, I would have brought her away with me." Thinks herself his daughter. Became convent scholar; received pupil garb. Valjean succeeded getting nuns restore mourning suit from Thénardier departure; locked up these garments plus stockings/shoes with camphor/aromatics in little valise; procured valise, set on chair near bed; always carried key. Cosette asked: "Father, what is there in that box which smells so good?" At appointed hour flies to hut filling it with paradise; adored him because sisters melancholy and he kind.

## Fauchelevent's Role and Current Status

**Identity**: Old crippled gardener admitted approximately two years previously (1821 or earlier) on Valjean's (Mayor Madeleine's) recommendation after cart accident. Limps; takes nearly quarter hour traversing short distances; complains aching back as usual.

**EXECUTION OF PLANS**: Used service door placing Cosette in vintage basket, left with deaf fruit-seller in Rue Chemin-Vert. Placed Valjean in coffin; transported in hearse to Vaugirard cemetery. At cemetery, Father Mestienne (grave-digger) dead; replaced by "little Father Lenoir" (jug red wine). Grave-digger lost card. Fauchelevent found card, buried corpse, filled grave himself.

**CHARACTER**: Grateful, talkative, excitable; calls Valjean "Father Madeleine"; peasant of Picardy. Perceived generous action as dying man perceives good wine. Old egoist finding sweetness in gratitude. Air of convent destroyed personal selfishness; rendered good action absolutely necessary.

**CURRENT STATUS**: Lives in garden hut with Valjean; continues gardening; sole person aware of Valjean and Cosette's full presence; only known ally/protector. Nuns do not suspect him; eyes fixed on God do not spy.

## Javert's Pursuit and Investigation Status

**REASSIGNMENT AND REACTIVATION**: When Valjean escaped M. sur M. jail (January 1823), Javert attached to Paris police. Newspaper announced Valjean's death (December 1823); Javert remarked "That's a good entry." Police report concerning child abduction in Montfermeil revived memory; suspected Valjean sought daughter.

**SECRET INVESTIGATION**: Without telling anyone, took coach to Montfermeil; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; hired room, listened at lodger's door; Valjean foiled spy by silence.

**REASONS FOR SECRECY**: (1) Slightest indiscretion might alert Valjean; (2) Recapturing ex-convict reputed dead magnificent success; (3) Javert had taste for unforeseen.

**PURSUIT ESCALATION**: Old woman suspected lodger intending to leave, warned Javert; Javert waited behind trees with two men at night. **Escape from Mouffetard**: Valjean cut street lantern rope; Javert found disorder, led astray. Followed from tree to tree; did not arrest hastily.

**CURRENT STATUS** (Spring-Summer Year 3): Even when saw Valjean escaped, sure convict could not be far off; established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades.

## M. Gillenormand and His World

**IDENTITY**: Worthy man; ancient inhabitants of Rue Boucherat, Rue de Normandie, Rue de Saintonge preserve his memory. Silhouette not yet entirely disappeared from labyrinth of streets near Temple.

**PHILOSOPHY AND HABITS**: Uttered frequently "the sensible man" and "nature." Gave nature his own acceptation in chimney-corner satires about barbarism, civilization as specimens, cat/tiger, lizard/crocodile analogies. Principal invariable habit: kept door absolutely closed during day, never received anyone except evening. Dined at five o'clock; after that door open. "Day is vulgar, deserves only closed shutter. Fashionable people only light up minds when zenith lights stars." Barricaded against everyone, even king. Antiquated elegance of his day.

**BOYHOOD HONORS**: Took prizes at College of Moulins (birthplace); crowned by hand of Duc de Nivernais (whom he called Duc de Nevers). Neither Convention, death of Louis XVI, Napoleon, Bourbon return erased this memory.

**SOCIAL DOMINATION**: Lived in Rue Servandoni (past residence), frequented many very good aristocratic salons. Although bourgeois, received in society. Had double measure of wit (born with him, then attributed to him); even sought out and made much of. Never went anywhere except on condition of being chief person there. Domination in Royalist salons cost his self-respect nothing. He was oracle everywhere. Held own against M. de Bonald and M. Bengy-Puy-Vallée.

**TWO DAUGHTERS**: Came into world ten years apart; in youth bore little resemblance. **Youngest**: Charming soul turned towards light, occupied with flowers, verses, music, fluttered into glorious space, enthusiastic, ethereal; wedded from youth in ideal to vague heroic figure. **Eldest** (Mademoiselle Gillenormand, the elder): Espied in azure wealthy purveyor/contractor/prefect; Prefecture receptions, usher with chain, official balls, town-hall harangues, being "Madame la Préfète"—whirlwind in imagination. Both strayed in own dreams as young girls. Both had wings—one like angel, other like goose.

**MADEMOISELLE GILLENORMAND, THE ELDER**: Antique virtue, incombustible prude, one of sharpest noses and most obtuse minds. Outside immediate family, no one knew first name. Age accentuated pitiless modesty; guimpe never sufficiently opaque; multiplied clasps/pins where no one would dream looking. Peculiarity of prudery: place more sentinels as fortress less menaced. To prudery added bigotry. Belonged to society of Virgin; wore white veil on festivals; mumbled special orisons; revered "holy blood," venerated "sacred heart"; remained hours contemplating rococo-jesuit altar in inaccessible chapel; allowed soul soar among marble clouds and gilded wood rays. Had chapel friend, ancient virgin Mademoiselle Vaubois (positive blockhead); beyond Agnus Dei/Ave Maria, Vaubois knew nothing except preserves-making. Ermine of stupidity without single spot intelligence. Gained rather than lost as grew older; never malicious (relative kindness); years wore away angles; softening came to her. Melancholy with obscure sadness of which she knew not secret. Breathed from whole person stupor of life finished, never had beginning. Kept house for father; household of old man and old spinster touching aspect of two weaknesses leaning for support.

**CHILD IN HOUSEHOLD**: Little boy always trembling and mute in presence of M. Gillenormand. Gillenormand never addressed child except in severe voice, sometimes with uplifted cane: "Here, sir! rascal, scoundrel, come here!—Answer me, you scamp! Just let me see you, you good-for-nothing!" etc. He idolized him.

**SALON CONNECTIONS (circa 1817)**: Invariably passed two afternoons weekly in **Rue Férou house** with **Madame la Baronne de T.**, worthy respectable person whose husband (Baron de T.) was Ambassador of France to Berlin under Louis XVI. Baron had died bankrupt during emigration, leaving curious Memoirs about Mesmer and his tub (ten manuscript volumes, red morocco, gilded edges). Madame de T. maintained herself on meagre surviving income; lived far from Court in "very mixed society," noble isolation, proud and poor. Constituted purely Royalist salon where few friends assembled twice weekly; sipped tea; uttered groans/horror at century, charter, Bonapartists, blue ribbon prostitution, Louis XVIII Jacobinism; spoke low tones of hopes presented by Monsieur, afterwards Charles X. Drew up lists of chamber of peers ("abominably Jacobin chamber"), combined alliances of names forming phrases like: _Damas. Sabran. Gouvion-Saint-Cyr_. Parodied Revolution; used desires give point to wrath in inverse sense; sang little _Ça ira_. Madame de T.'s salon had two cocks: M. Gillenormand and Comte de Lamothe-Valois (of infamous necklace affair); whispered with respect about Lamothe. Such singular amnesties do occur in parties.

## Narrative Themes and Authorial Commentary

**AUDACITY AND REVOLUTION**: All sublime conquests are prizes of daring. For Revolution to take place, insufficient that Montesquieu foresee, Diderot preach, Beaumarchais announce, Condorcet calculate, Arouet prepare, Rousseau premeditate; necessary that Danton dare. Cry "Audacity!" is "Fiat lux." Necessary for forward march that proud lessons of courage permanently on heights. Daring deeds dazzle history. Attempt, brave, persist, persevere—that is example nations need, light electrifying them.
